newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark pullback seen buying opportunity.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark pullback seen buying opportunity.

text.p: Dollar/mark's decline from Tuesday's 1.6570 high is a temporary dip and the retracement presents an excellent opportunity to refresh longs before new highs, technical analysts said.
Support near 1.6455 marks, the previous 31-month high exceeded on Monday, should remain intact. But if it breaks, technicians said they would not hesitate to scoop up dollars.
"If we close below 1.6450 marks it could move down to 1.6300, that would be a spectacular buy," said Randolph Donney, director of capital market research at Pegasus Econometric Group.

Al Inglesino, technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch, said he looked for an initial move down to between 1.6450 and 1.6405, ahead of another bounce higher. But he said a break below 1.6365 could delay the rebound.
"If we get below this (1.6365) level, then I'm looking for a possible deferral of the bullish potential; maybe we get to 1.6200 (marks), the pullback is a little deeper," he added.

The medium-to-longer term outlook for the dollar remains decidedly bullish, analysts said. Above Tuesday's 31-month high, Inglesino placed the next objectives within a 1.6720 to 1.6820 "resistance window".
Donney said the dollar could reach 1.71 marks by April.

Many daily and weekly technical studies, such as the relative strength index, are overbought. Moving average convergence studies are also topping out, but analysts said while these may foreshadow an eventual correction of the rally, the dollar's uptrend is still too strong to heed them.
Analysts also remain strongly bullish dollar/yen after Tuesday's sharp rise, despite similarly overbought technical indicators.
"We're overbought in just about every possible way you could imagine in dollar/yen," Donney said. "But I don't want to go against this trend, there is too much behind it."
The medium-term upside target in dollar/yen is 123.50 but intermediate resistance should be encountered at 121.95 and 122.55, according to analysts.
Support lies at 120.60 yen, followed by 119.25, they said.
At 1400 EST on Tuesday, dollar/yen was trading at 121.68/78 up from 120.64/69 at the U.S. open and at 1.6525/35 marks, up from 1.6508/13.
